questions.question_text: A rectangular rug is $2.4\text{ m}$ long and $1.5\text{ m}$ wide. Find the area of the rug in $\text{m}^{2}$.

options.why: Found the perimeter $2(2.4+1.5)$ instead of multiplying the two side lengths.
Added the length and the width instead of multiplying them.
Halved the product, applying the triangle rule instead of $A=lw$.
Found both areas correctly but named the smaller value, $40\text{ cm}^{2}$, as the larger one.
Added the side lengths, $10+4$ and $7+7$, which both give $14$, instead of multiplying them.
Compared shape B’s area of $49$ with shape A’s perimeter of $28\text{ cm}$.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{\text{A}}=10\times4$
$=40\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{\text{B}}=7\times7$
$=49\text{ cm}^{2}$
$49-40=9$
Shape B has the larger area, by $9\text{ cm}^{2}$.
